facts.label: Passado e comparativos
facts.sub: Conte o passado com verbos regulares e irregulares: I ordered your chicken. Compare com -er than: It was sweeter than my mom’s chicken.

facts.label: Passado
facts.sub: Para contar o que aconteceu, use o passado simples: I ordered your chicken. Verbos regulares ganham -ed: visited, mixed, cooked. Alguns são irregulares.

facts.label: Comparar
facts.sub: Para comparar adjetivos curtos, use -er + than: sweeter than, softer than, fresher than, cheaper than. Compare duas coisas ou dois lugares.

pages.title: A busy kitchen · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm evening in a busy restaurant kitchen in Atlanta. Pots hiss on the stove. Zoe stands at the kitchen door with a smile. Her friend Walt is the chef. He wears a tall white hat. He says hello over the noise.
“Hi, Zoe! You visited my restaurant last night.” says Walt. “Yes! I ordered your chicken. It was sweeter than my mom’s chicken.” says Zoe. “Ha! Did you like it? What was the secret?” says Walt.
